title: Markdown Header Chunker
prompt:
Implement `chunk_markdown(markdown, max_chars)`.

Split a Markdown document into chunks whose Python `len()` is at most `max_chars`. Normalize CRLF and CR newlines to LF before processing.

Use ATX headings (`#` through `######`) to maintain a level-aware active header stack. Ignore heading-looking lines inside fenced code blocks delimited by lines starting with triple backticks. When a new chunk starts inside a section, prefix the active headers in order, followed by a blank line, so the chunk keeps section context. This synthetic header context counts toward `max_chars`.

Prefer splitting on blank-line paragraph boundaries. If a paragraph or line is too large, split it by character budget and repeat the active header context for every continuation chunk. If the required header context alone cannot fit in `max_chars`, raise a `ValueError`. If `max_chars <= 0`, raise a `ValueError`.

example.input:
markdown = '# Guide

## Install

First paragraph.

Second paragraph.', max_chars = 40
example.output:
['# Guide

## Install

First paragraph.', '# Guide
## Install

Second paragraph.']
example.reasoning: The second chunk starts inside the Install section, so it repeats the active parent headers.
